title: Your teacher “shared a private file”
scenario: An email that looks like it came from a teacher says, “I added comments to your draft—open before class.” The link asks you to approve a new app to read your school files and email.

answers.A: Approve the app because the teacher really is reviewing your draft this week.
answers.B: Open the school drive/LMS yourself and look for the shared file there, or ask the teacher directly.
answers.C: Check the sender address carefully and ask a classmate whether they received the same message.

explanation: A believable teacher context can hide an OAuth permission request that grants broad access without stealing your password.
proTip: “Approve access” can be as powerful as “enter password.”
